# dsh-provider-pool
A DeepSeek Harness plugin: a **local OpenAI-compatible proxy** with a **prioritized provider pool an
d automatic fallback**.
Point any DSH custom model at `http://127.0.0.1:3121/v1` once. Every request is then tried against y
our providers in priority order — if one is rate-limited, out of credit, down, or too slow, the next
one is used automatically. The provider API keys stay on the host; the browser UI only ever sees th
e last 4 characters.
> Status: `0.1.0` (MVP). Local-only, no npm publish, no network telemetry.
## Features

- **Local proxy** — `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1`, OpenAI compatible:
- `POST /v1/chat/completio

ns` (streaming and non-streaming)
- `GET /v1/models` (aggregates the provider model lists, failures

ignored)
- `GET /health`
- **Automatic fallback** — tries providers by `priority` (smaller first):
-

non-streaming: fallback on `401 / 402 / 403 / 429 / 5xx`, connection errors and **20 s timeout**;
-
streaming: fallback only **before the first upstream byte** (response headers); once SSE bytes are

flowing the response is committed and never switched mid-stream;
- other `4xx` (e.g. `400`, `404`) a

re passed through unchanged, so your request bugs are not silently masked.
- **Port fallback** — con

figured port (default `3121`), if busy tries `3122 … 3130` automatically.
- **Call log** — every att
empt (`time, providerId, model, ms, status, fallback, stream`) is kept in memory (last 200) and pers

isted to `~/.dsh/provider-pool-stats.json`.
- **Panel** — sidebar entry + full-screen panel rendered
with **React directly (no iframe)**: provider list, add/edit/delete, connectivity test, recent-call

stats, proxy address with copy button.
- **Key hygiene** — API keys are used only on the host, mask
ed as `••••abcd` everywhere, and never written to logs or stats files.

After the restart you should see **🔀 Provider Pool** at the bottom of the left sidebar.

1. Open the panel (🔀 in the sidebar) and add at least one provider, or create

2. In DSH model settings add a **custom OpenAI-compatible provider**:
- Base URL: `http://127.0.0.1:

3121/v1` (copy it from the panel)
- API Key: anything (ignored — the proxy uses the pooled keys)
- M

odel: anything (if a provider has `model` set, the proxy rewrites the request model to it;
otherwise
the requested model is forwarded unchanged)
3. Chat as usual. If the first provider returns `500`/`429`/`401` or times out, the panel stats show

the
fallback attempt and the answer comes from the next provider.
## Configuration (`~/.dsh/provider-pool.json`)
| Field | Default | Description |
| `proxyPort` | `3121` | Local proxy port. If busy, `3122 … 3130` are tried; the actually used port

is shown in the panel. |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | Per-provider timeout until the upstream response

headers arrive. |
| `providers[]` | `[]` | Provider list, sorted by `priority`. |
| `providers[].id`

| auto | Stable id (auto-generated from the name when added via the panel). |
| `providers[].name`

| — | Display name. |
| `providers[].baseUrl` | — | `http(s)://…`; `/v1/chat/completions` is appende

d automatically, or used directly if the URL already ends in `/v1`. |
| `providers[].apiKey` | `""`

| Bearer token. **Host-only**, never sent to the browser. |
| `providers[].model` | `""` | If set, t

he request model is rewritten to this value before forwarding. |
| `providers[].priority` | insertio
n order | Smaller number = tried earlier. |

The file is read on every request, so provider edits in the panel take effect immediately.
A changed
`proxyPort` needs a DSH restart (the listener is created when the plugin loads).
## Panel API
Registered on the host `connection` service (same-origin, authenticated by DSH) under `/api/dsh-prov
on the host `connection` service (same-origin, authenticated by DSH) under `/api/dsh-provider-pool`:
| Route | Description |

| `GET /list` | Providers with masked keys, proxy state, config path, warnings |
[该节后续省略]
## Security model

- The proxy binds `127.0.0.1` only and is not exposed to the network.
- The proxy replaces any incom

ing `Authorization` header with the pooled provider key.
The key never reaches the browser: `/list`,

`/test`, `/stats` only return `••••` + last 4 characters.
- Stats and error messages are sanitized;

stats files never contain keys.
- `~/.dsh/provider-pool.json` holds plaintext keys: on POSIX it is

written with mode `600`
(Windows ignores the mode — protect the file with your user profile ACL).
-

The proxy itself does not authenticate callers; any local process can call it.
That is the same trus
t level as the DSH process itself.
## Known limitations
- **Streaming switch boundary**: fallback can only happen before the first upstream byte. If a provi

der
accepts the request, starts streaming, and then dies mid-stream, the client response is terminat

ed
rather than silently resumed from another provider (mixing two SSE streams would corrupt the answ

er).
- Fallback triggers are limited to `401 / 402 / 403 / 429 / 5xx`, network errors and timeouts;

other `4xx` are returned as-is by design.
- `ms` in the stats is time-to-decision: for non-streaming

it is the full response time, for streaming it
is the first-byte latency (the stream itself can run

if all ports `3121–3130` are busy the proxy stays down and the
panel shows the error (the plugin it

self keeps working).
- No vision/embedding/rerank routing yet — chat completions and model listing o

keeps working).
- No vision/embedding/rerank routing yet — chat completions and model listing only.
